[New chat] George Adams, order HP-20890. How should I look after the outdoor bench over the winter?

Hi George — happy to help. Here are simple, effective steps to protect an outdoor bench over winter. If you tell me the bench material (e.g., teak, oak, pine, painted wood, or metal) I can give more specific product recommendations.

Before winter (best done before the first hard freeze)
- Clean: remove leaves/debris, brush off loose dirt. Wipe with a mild detergent solution, rinse, and let fully dry.
- Tighten hardware: check and tighten bolts/screws; replace any badly corroded fasteners.
- Treat the surface:
  - Untreated or softwood (pine, spruce): apply an exterior wood preservative or clear water‑repellent sealer, or an exterior oil/stain designed for decking/furniture.
  - Teak or dense hardwood: you can leave it to silver naturally, or apply teak oil/maintenance product if you prefer the golden colour.
  - Painted/finished wood: touch up scratched areas with matching exterior paint or varnish to seal exposed grain.
  - Metal: remove surface rust with a wire brush and touch up with rust primer + suitable topcoat.
- Protect cushions: bring cushions/ pads indoors or store in a dry shed/garage. If leaving them out, use a breathable storage bag; do not trap moisture.

During winter
- Use a breathable cover (furniture cover or canvas) to keep precipitation off but allow moisture to escape. Avoid tight non‑breathable plastic that can trap condensation and cause rot.
- Elevate slightly: if possible, raise legs off wet ground with small blocks so water can’t pool under legs.
- Clear snow and ice promptly with a soft brush — don’t chip at ice or use rock salt on nearby surfaces that could corrode metal or strip finishes.
- Periodic checks: if storms are frequent, check the bench occasionally and remove heavy snow.

After winter
- Remove cover, clean again, inspect for damage (loose joints, splits, rust) and repair as needed.
- Refinish or re‑oil any areas that look dry or weathered.

If you tell me the bench model or the material (or give your order number), I’ll send tailored care steps and product suggestions — or I can add a note to your order with the care instructions.

Yes — please register your son on our Priority Services Register (PSR). If he relies on a home oxygen machine, PSR gives you extra support and helps us prioritise you in an outage or other emergency.

Benefits of PSR
- priority help and updates during power outages and planned work (so restoration is prioritised where possible)
- advance notice of planned interruptions
- a nominated contact we can call if we can’t reach you
- meter-reading and billing support (e.g. alternative formats, large print, email/post preferences)
- password/security scheme for callers and visits
- assistance arranging alternative power solutions where available
- we’ll record medical dependency so staff and engineers know the situation

What we need to register
- confirmation that your son uses a home oxygen machine (brief description: “oxygen concentrator” or “portable oxygen”)
- whether it needs mains power continuously or only sometimes
- best contact number(s) and email, and a nominated emergency contact (name & number)
- preferred communication method (phone / SMS / email / post) and any accessibility needs (large print, translator, etc.)
- permission to record medical dependency on the account (this stays confidential)

Safety notes (important)
- PSR helps with priority support but is not a guarantee of continuous power — please have a clinical contingency plan (e.g. backup cylinders, battery backup, or plan with healthcare provider).
- If you have immediate worries about equipment function or safety, contact your healthcare provider or emergency services.

Would you like me to register him now? If so, please confirm:
1) Equipment type (e.g. “home oxygen concentrator”), and whether it requires mains power continuously.  
2) Best phone and email and a nominated contact (name & phone).  
3) Preferred contact method and any special needs.  
4) Your consent for us to add this to the account.

If you prefer, I can start the registration and then we’ll follow up to confirm details.

[New chat] Yusuf Ali, BW-431120. I want to add my wife Amira as a second account holder. How do I do that?

I can help with that. To add Amira as a second (co-)account holder we’ll need to verify identity and get her consent — here’s what to expect and the options so you can choose the easiest for you.

What adding a second account holder means
- Amira will have the same rights as you on the account: access to bills and meter readings, ability to make changes (tariff, direct debit), and responsibility for payments.
- We’ll record her as a named account holder on BW-431120.

What we need to add her
- Confirmation that you (the current account holder) agree to add her.
- Amira’s details: full name, date of birth, and best phone number and email.
- Proof of identity for Amira (one of: passport, driving licence, national ID).
- Proof of address if different from the account address (recent utility bill or bank statement dated within last 3 months). If she lives at the same address, we usually don’t need extra address proof.
- Her consent (signed or submitted via our secure online form, or given verbally and recorded during a verification call).

How to complete it (choose one)
1) Quick secure form (recommended)
   - I can send a secure link to Amira’s email/phone so she can upload ID and give consent. This is the fastest method and usually completed within 1–2 business days.

2) Start it here by chat
   - Tell me Amira’s full name, DOB, and preferred contact and confirm you consent. I’ll add a note and our team will call you both to verify and complete the addition.

3) Phone verification/signature
   - We can schedule a short verification call at a convenient time for you and Amira. During the call we’ll confirm ID details and record consent.

Other things to consider
- If you don’t want her to have full account control, you can instead add her as a nominated contact (for notifications only) — let me know if that’s preferable.
- Adding a second holder doesn’t change the account balance or payment arrangements unless you ask us to.

What would you like to do now?
- I can send the secure link to Amira (please give her email or mobile), or
- I can start the process and add a note that you requested this (and then arrange a verification call), or
- I can explain how to upload documents if you prefer to do that yourself.
